# SK1084 — Use a LINQ operator for part of the loop

<!-- Generated from Rules/Rikarin.Skala.Rules.Metadata/rules.json. Do not edit. -->

A `foreach` whose entire body is one `if` is a filter and a loop wearing one construct; the filter can move to the sequence.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | Modernization |
| Default severity | hint |
| Scope | Semantic |
| Needs a compilation | yes |
| Fix | yes, review it |
| Language version floor | — |
| Since | 2.0 |

## Why

The loop header says *what is visited* and the body says *what is done*, and a body that is nothing but a guard has put half of the first sentence into the second. Moving the guard to the sequence leaves each construct saying one thing, and it puts the condition next to the thing being filtered rather than one indent below the thing being processed. It is the smallest of this range's rewrites and the one most likely to be declined on taste, which is why it ships at `hint`.

## Example

Instead of:

```csharp
foreach (var entry in entries) {
    if (entry.IsVisible) {
        Render(entry);
    }
}
```

Write:

```csharp
foreach (var entry in entries.Where(entry => entry.IsVisible)) {
    Render(entry);
}
```

## When it does not fire

⚠ **`Where` is lazy, and that is the whole equivalence argument rather than a detail of it.** `Where`'s `MoveNext` pulls one element, evaluates the predicate and yields, so the predicate for element *n* runs after the body for element *n-1* and immediately before the body for element *n* — the same interleaving, in the same order, the same number of times, as the `if` it replaced. A condition that reads state the body mutates therefore still sees exactly what it saw. ⚠ **A `break`, a `continue` or a `return` in the body does not prevent this rewrite, and the belief that it does is what kept the shape looking unshippable.** Only the *filter* moves; the body stays a loop body, so `continue` still advances the same `foreach` and `break` still leaves it. What a `break` does change is how many times the predicate runs — it stops early either way, at the same element. ⚠ The body must be exactly one `if` with no `else` and no other statement, and the condition must mention the loop variable, or the "filter" is a constant the reader would rather see hoisted. ⚠ **The condition has to be liftable into a lambda, which is a compile question and is asked as one**: a condition declaring a pattern variable the body then uses is refused, because the declaration would move out of scope, and so is one that reads a `ref`, `out` or `in` parameter, a ref local, a `ref struct` local, `stackalloc`, a pointer, or `this` inside a struct — each of those is a lambda the compiler rejects, and a fix that does not compile is worse than the shape it replaced. `await` and `yield` in the condition are impossible by construction and are excluded anyway. ⚠ `System.Linq` must already be imported: the fix does not add a using directive, so a file without one is left alone rather than broken. An `await foreach` is a different operator and is not covered. ⚠ **It is the one rule in this range that suggests LINQ, so it declares the interaction rather than leaving it to be discovered.** `SK4006` reports a materialization consumed by `foreach` and this fix produces no materialization, so it cannot feed that rule; `SK4001` reports LINQ in a configured hot path, and there the two genuinely disagree — which is settled by this rule shipping at `hint`, one step below anything `SK4001` says, so a repository that configures a hot path keeps the loop. ⚠ `fixIsSafe` is false: the rewrite allocates an iterator and a delegate the loop did not, and that is a decision about the call site rather than about the shape.
